parts:
I usually use multipart/form-data and then pass the json as an post argument. In that case you can grab it from the POST object in rapache, and I have never had any trouble with that.

I have never used receiveBin. It seems to have a length argument? You might need to set this? The SERVER object seems to have some values, e.g. read_length that might be related?

Let us know what you find :)
On Sun, Mar 17, 2013 at 7:47 PM, Andrew Schreiber <schre...@gmail.com> wrote:

I have a javascript file that sends a json object to the server for processing with an R script. I can get this to work fine with smaller datasets (i.e smaller json objects) but when I send a longer json object to the server, it is not recognizing the object as valid json.

Is there a maximum length for json objects when using Rapache or RJSONIO?

Please let meknow if anyone has experienced enything similar or has any thoughts.

Thanks,

Andrew

Here is a sample from my R script:

# supposedly loads all installed packages...
lapply(.packages(all.available = TRUE), function(xx) library(xx,     character.only = TRUE))

binpost  <- receiveBin()
postdata <- rawToChar(binpost)

 if (isValidJSON(postdata, TRUE)) {

   v <- "looks like valid json"
   
 } else {

    v <- "looks NOT like valid json"
   
    resdata <- toJSON(v)
    cat(resdata)
 }

... and the javascript (where 'formdata' should be valid json)

$.ajax({
            type: "POST",
            url: "http://localhost/povApp/rscripts/regression.r",
            data: formdata,
            contentType: "application/json" 
         });
 
         $("#result").ajaxSuccess(function(event, xhr, settings) {
            $(this).text('IT WORKS!!!' + xhr.responseText );
            console.log(xhr.responseText);
         });
         $("#result").ajaxError(function(event, xhr, settings) {
            $(this).text("Request failed");
         });

Thanks again.

On Mon, Mar 18, 2013 at 5:51 PM, Andrew Schreiber <schre...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Regarding the use of the POST object, do you know what syntax would be used in R to get the data when passed as a jQuery ajax request rather than as a form? (i.e. thedata <- str(POST) - this always returns 'null') ?

jQuery will use multipart/form-data encoding by default for ajax
requests if you do not set the "contentType" argument in your $.ajax()
call.

Try something like:

data: {"mydata" : JSON.stringify(formdata) }
});

That should give you a POST$mydata in rapache.
